text:
maria_p: Heads-up — incoming customer report from AcmePay: after the v3.3 model rollout some function/tool invocations are failing with schema errors. ticket #4532. :rotating_light:

alex_w: saw the same in canary logs earlier, small spike in tool-schema-failures. linking trace: https://rwd.in/trace/abc123

deploy-bot: rollout started: redwood-model-3.2 -> redwood-model-3.3, batch id batch-2024-07-01-09:14

josh_t: paste of failing request/response from customer (redacted) — they call the hosted API with a tool call for `charge_card`:
```
POST /v1/invoke
{
  "model": "redwood-model-3.3",
  "input": "Charge $12.50 for order 987",
  "functions": [{"name":"charge_card","parameters":{"card_number":"****","amount":"12.50","currency":"USD"}}]
}
```

josh_t: error returned:
```
{"error":{"type":"tool_schema_error","message":"missing required property: amount_cents","details":"expected integer 'amount_cents' but got missing"}}
```

maria_p: interesting — previous model variant (3.2) would map `amount` -> `amount_cents` (int) automatically in the generated function args. 3.3 is emitting different param names and string amounts. That matches customer repro where arg is string and wrong key.

alex_w: also seeing an uptick in 5xx and billing anomalies (customers retried multiple times). SRE dashboard: 5xx rates +1.8%, token costs up due to retries. @sre_oncall can you confirm infra impact?

sre_oncall: confirmed increased tail-latency on the function-invoke path and a few CPU spikes on the JSON validator pods. Not a networking ACL or auth issue. No new IAM errors.

support-bot: customer note: "After your recent update, our checkout fails intermittently with Tool schema validation errors. We can't complete payments. Please advise ASAP."

maria_p: this reads like a model-level behavioral regression in the function-calling codegen. Probably a change in the model prompt template or a mismatch with the function schema normalization step. Repro steps I ran locally against 3.3:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/invoke \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-model-3.3","input":"Charge $1.00","functions":[{"name":"charge_card","parameters":{"card_number":"****","amount":"1.00","currency":"USD"}}]}'
```
=> returns tool_schema_error (missing amount_cents)

alex_w: repro against 3.2 returns successful JSON arguments with `amount_cents":100` and call proceeds to payment gateway. So it's definitely model-variant-specific.

eng-runtime: quick note — the runtime validates function args against declared JSON schema. If the model emits a different shape or string-typed amount, the runtime rejects it. We could consider a permissive coercion layer but that's risky for payments.

maria_p: immediate ask: can we rollback the model rollout to 3.2 for the affected customers/segments and pin redwood-model-3.3 behind a hold?

deploy-bot: canary traffic accounted: 3.3 at 22% overall, affected customers flagged: AcmePay (enterprise), several self-serve tenants.

josh_t: mitigation options: 1) quick rollback to 3.2 for all traffic 2) patch runtime to coerce `amount` string -> `amount_cents` int for charge_card only 3) soft-fix prompt mapping on model side. Runtime patch would be fastest but touches payments path and needs SOC review.

sre_oncall: given customer impact (payment failures), recommend rollback now and open a postmortem. Latency/billing hit will continue if we leave 3.3 in.

alex_w: +1 rollback. Eng-runtime and product to follow up for a safer re-release.

maria_p: on it — opening a rollback runbook with priority escalate. Notifying AcmePay support rep with ETA.

eng-runtime: I'll create an issue with examples and attach traces. We should include: sample payloads (3.2 vs 3.3), execution logs, and failing schema validator output.

support-bot: customer replied: "Thank you. We'll wait for your rollback. This is impacting live checkout." :sadpanda:

deploy-bot: initiating rollback to redwood-model-3.2 for affected tenants. rollback-id rb-2024-07-01-09:22

maria_p: logging action and assigning to eng-runtime (P0) for root cause. tagging legal/compliance because it's payment-impacting.

josh_t: after rollback verify: please run regression hooks and a short canary with synthetic payment calls so we get green before full re-release.

eng-runtime: agreed. Will run head-to-head diff tests and surface the prompt->arg mapping diffs. I'll also produce a minimal test that asserts `amount_cents` presence for charge_card calls.

maria_p: summary: rollback in progress, customer notified, P0 bug filed, follow-up postmortem planned.  Will update thread when rollback completes. :thumbsup:
